text: Thank you, Madam Clerk. I wanna thank everybody to, wanna welcome everybody to our council meeting. speaker: racheltyczinski
text: There are several proclamations. Under agenda item 5.1 is motorcycle awareness month.

speaker: provenzano
text: Thank you, Madam Clerk. Whereas the motorcycle is an important part of recreation and transportation in Canada and it's played supporting roles with our military and law enforcement agencies. And whereas in 2017, there were 721,000 motorcycle and scooters registered in Canada with 217,049 or 31.4% of those in Ontario. Whereas 164 motorcycle enthusiasts were killed on Ontario city streets and highways since 2011 to date. And awareness of sharing the road with all users can assist in the reduction of these fatalities. Whereas the Sault Ste. Marie Bikers Rights Organization region 22, which is to promote the education, safe riding habits for motorcycles and motorcycle awareness on our city streets. Now, therefore I, Christian Provenzan was married to the city of Sault Ste. Marie do hereby proclaim May 2021 as Sault Ste. Marie Motorcycle Awareness Month in the city of Sault Ste. Marie. Thank you.

speaker: racheltyczinski
text: Under agenda item 5.2, melanoma and skin cancer awareness month.

speaker: provenzano
text: So I have a proclamation here. Whereas it is imperative that communities across Canada recognize the importance of sun safety and overexposure to UV radiation is one of the major causes of melanoma and non-melanoma skin cancers. Whereas skin cancers are the most common of all cancers and one in six Canadians born in the 1990s will get skin cancer in their lifetimes. Whereas many people seek sun without taking the recommended precautionary measures and aren't aware that any darkening of skin color, including a tan is indicative of UV damage. Whereas self skin examinations should be performed on a monthly basis because skin cancers are highly treatable when detected early. Whereas Save Your Skin Foundation is dedicated to the fight against non-melanoma skin cancers, melanoma and ocular melanoma through nationwide education advocacy and awareness initiatives. And therefore I, Christian Provenzanos, Mayor of the city of Sault Ste. Marie hereby declare the month of May, 2021 is melanoma and skin cancer awareness month in the city of Sault Ste. Marie.

speaker: racheltyczinski
text: Under item 5.3, community living awareness month.

speaker: provenzano
text: Thank you, Madam Clerk. Community Living Algoma has provided supports and services to people with intellectual disabilities and their families in the city of Sault Ste. Marie and surrounding districts since 1954. We currently provide service to 333 adults and 388 children. Whereas Community Living Algoma's goal is that people with intellectual disabilities have every opportunity to participate fully in our community with dignity, independence and acceptance. Whereas Community Living Algoma works with Sault Ste. Marie volunteers and other stakeholder groups and organizations to promote citizenship for people with intellectual disabilities. So they have the rights and responsibilities and the opportunities that come with belonging, participating and contributing as valued members in society. Whereas Community Living Awareness Month is a province-wide initiative created to celebrate the values of community living, which are inclusion, quality and respect. And therefore I, Mayor Christian Provenzanos, Mayor of the city of Sault Ste. Marie do hereby proclaim May, 2021 to be Community Living Awareness Month in the city of Sault Ste. Marie.

speaker: racheltyczinski
text: Under agenda item 5.4, Children's Mental Health Week.

speaker: provenzano
text: Whereas one in five Canadians struggle with their mental health and this has been exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. Whereas ensuring the mental health of our children, youth and adults is essential to overall wellbeing, growth and development, particularly during the pandemic shutdowns and the isolations this creates. Whereas mental health challenges can include addiction, depression, anxiety, eating disorders, conduct disorders, attention deficit, hyperactivity disorder, schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. Whereas many who benefit from mental health services are finding more services online and in-person through Algonquin Family Services, Surrey Hospital, Algonquin Public Health, the John Howard Society and the Canadian Mental Health Association. Whereas learning to recognize the early warning signs of mental health challenges and where to obtain necessary assistance and treatment gives families better opportunities to lead productive lives. And therefore I, Christian Provenzanos, Mayor of the City of Sault Ste. Marie do hereby proclaim May 3rd to May 9th, 2021 as Children's and Youth Mental Health Week and Mental Health Week. We acknowledge Dr. Winderman, Thrive, Strong Minds, CHME, MA Algoma, Long McQuaid along with Algoma Family Services for their efforts in bringing attention to this important week. We encourage all citizens of Sault Ste. Marie to work together and raise awareness of the mental health needs in our community.

speaker: racheltyczinski
text: And item 5.5, Young Professionals Week.

speaker: provenzano
text: So whereas Thrive Young Professionals Group works to build and promote professional development, community involvement and networking opportunities in Sault Ste. Marie. And whereas the Young Professionals Network of Ontario has historically proclaimed the second week in May a Young Professionals Week in the province of Ontario. Whereas Thrive aims to increase advocacy and awareness surrounding young professionals in the community, including retention and attraction in Sault Ste. Marie. It wants to recognize resiliency and tenacity displayed by young professionals throughout the COVID-19 pandemic. Whereas Young Professionals Week will provide an opportunity for young professionals to connect, network and build relationships and lean on each other to help foster a stronger community and a stronger future for Sault Ste. Marie. And therefore I, Christian Provenzanos, Mayor of the City of Sault Ste. Marie do hereby proclaim and pronounce the week of May 9th and May 15th, 2021 as Young Professionals Week here in Sault Ste. Marie. And ask that the community come together to support our local young professionals and entrepreneurs. And the endeavours of the members of our council will strive Young Professionals Group. Thank you.

speaker: racheltyczinski
text: And agenda item 5.6, the National Day of Mourning.

speaker: provenzano
text: The National Day of Mourning is held annually on April 28th to commemorate workers who have been killed, injured or suffered illness due to workplace related hazards and incidents. Whereas the purpose of the Day of Mourning is to remember and honour those workers and to renew commitment to improve health and safety in the workplace. Whereas April 28th was chosen to be the National Day of Mourning as it coincides with the day the Workers' Compensation Act received its third reading in 1914. Whereas the Canadian flag on Parliament Hill will fly at half mass and workers and employers across Canada will observe this day by lighting candles, donning ribbons and black armbands and observing moments of silence. And therefore I, Christian Provenzand was made the City of Sault Ste. Marie to hereby proclaim April 28th, 2021 as the Day of Mourning in the City of Sault Ste. Marie in recognition of workers killed, injured or disabled on the job. Before we move on Madam Clerk to the consent agenda, I just want to recognize all the agencies that ask for these proclamations. And as we've been away from our meetings in person, one of the things I've really missed is seeing all of these groups come before our council and speak to the community and remind the community about their initiatives and who they are and what they're doing. And I've come to really value that part of our meeting. And I look forward to when it returns and when we can have our delegations and all the people across our community that are doing such great work exemplified by these proclamations in our council chambers, talking to the community at large and getting the community engaged in the issues that they're raising. On the same note council, I'll tell you that I do miss all of you. It's difficult to do this job from afar. And I know that a lot of us took a lot of joy and comfort in seeing each other every couple of weeks and having that proximity to one another as we kind of work through what we have to work through in leading our community and making decisions. And I want to thank all of you for making the effort that all of you have to kind of stay together as a group and continue to work together as we work through these times. It'd be much preferable to be with all of you. And I really look forward to the day where I get to see all of you again on the regular. And I'm hoping that's around the corner. So I just wanted to acknowledge all the people in our community who are doing good work and acknowledge each of the 10 of you for the work you're doing and the patience you're demonstrating through these times. I'm quite with that noted, we can move on to the consent agenda.
